question.problem: Given that ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1-18{x}^{2}}{12p{x}^{2}-3x+9}=-2,$  what is the value of $p?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1-18{x}^{2}}{12p{x}^{2}-3x+9} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{18{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{12p{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{3x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{9}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-18)}{(12p-\frac{3}{x}+\frac{9}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{0-18}{12p-0+0} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2p} & =-2 \\ 4p & =3 \\ p & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
